eventTypes.SAFETY_ADVISORY: Safety advisory (recommendation to operators; not a closure)
eventTypes.AIRSPACE_RESTRICTION: Official restriction of an airspace for some operators, aircraft, altitudes or times
eventTypes.AIRSPACE_CLOSURE: Officially confirmed closure of an airspace
eventTypes.AIRPORT_CLOSURE: Officially confirmed suspension of an airport's operations
eventTypes.SECURITY_INCIDENT: Military action, attack or security incident that may affect air traffic
eventTypes.AIRSPACE_REOPENING: Lifting of a restriction or closure (not a return to normal operations)
eventTypes.OTHER_VERIFIED_EVENT: Other event with a checkable source

note: Facts as stated by the sources. Relations marked basis=temporal are only closeness in time. Nothing here is a cause of an observed change.

events.title: Military strikes on Iran and Iranian retaliation
events.titleJa: イランへの軍事攻撃とイランの報復
events.description: EASA's bulletin states that on 28 February 2026 the United States and Israel conducted military strikes on sites in Iran and that Iran carried out retaliatory attacks.
events.documentType: statement in an aviation safety bulletin

occurrence.basis: date stated in EASA CZIB 2026-03; no time of day

sourceReferences.title: EASA CZIB 2026-03 (current page, R14): description of the conflict

verified: EASA (an aviation authority, not a party) states the date of the strikes and of the retaliation.
notVerified: No government statement of the parties was captured.
The time of day is not known.
Which places were struck is not recorded here.
events.confidenceNotes: Date only. Shown on the timeline as a whole day, not as 00:00 UTC.

events.title: Temporary US-Iran ceasefire announced
events.titleJa: 米国とイランの一時停戦の発表
events.description: EASA's bulletin states that a temporary ceasefire between the United States and Iran was initially announced on 8 April 2026 and remained in effect until 17 June 2026, when it was extended for 60 days by a memorandum of understanding.
events.documentType: statement in an aviation safety bulletin

occurrence.basis: date stated in EASA CZIB 2026-03 R14

sourceReferences.title: EASA CZIB 2026-03 (current page, R14): description of the conflict

verified: EASA states the announcement date (8 April) and the extension on 17 June.
notVerified: No statement of the parties was captured.
The time of the announcement is not known.

events.title: UAE: temporary and partial closure of the airspace (GCAA)
events.titleJa: UAE：空域の一時的・部分的な閉鎖（GCAA）
events.description: The Qatar News Agency reports that the UAE General Civil Aviation Authority announced the temporary and partial closure of UAE airspace as an exceptional precautionary measure.
events.documentType: statement relayed by a state news agency

publication.basis: publication time of the Khaleej Times article (an upper bound of the announcement time)

sourceReferences.title: UAE civil aviation temporarily, partially closes airspace
UAE temporarily and partially closes airspace after US, Israel strike Iran

verified: A state news agency reports the GCAA announcement of a temporary, partial closure on 28 February.
notVerified: The GCAA statement itself and the NOTAM were not captured.
Which parts of the airspace, which flights and from what time are not known.
When it ended is not known.
events.confidenceNotes: Partial closure: not all flights were prohibited according to the reports.

events.title: UAE: suspension of drones and light sport aircraft (GCAA Safety Decision 2026-03)
events.titleJa: UAE：無人機・軽スポーツ機の運航停止（GCAA 安全決定 2026-03）
events.description: GCAA Safety Decision 2026-03, issue 01, dated 28 February 2026, suspends with immediate effect all authorisations for unmanned aircraft systems and light sport aircraft and prohibits their operation in UAE airspace during the suspension period.

effectiveFrom.basis: 'effective immediately' on the date of issue; no time stated

affectedOperators.text: Operators of drones (commercial and recreational) and of light sport aircraft of all types

sourceReferences.title: GCAA Safety Decision 2026-03: temporary suspension of drones and light sport aircraft in UAE airspace

verified: The authority's own document states the suspension, its scope and its date of issue.
notVerified: The end of the suspension was not captured.
events.confidenceNotes: Applies to drones and light sport aircraft only; it is not a closure for airliners.

events.title: Qatar: temporary suspension of air navigation (QCAA), as reported
events.titleJa: カタール：航空交通の一時停止（QCAA、報道による）
events.description: The Peninsula reports that the Qatar Civil Aviation Authority announced the temporary suspension of air navigation in Qatari airspace as a precautionary step. On 7 March, IOL reported that the closure of Qatari airspace was continuing.

publication.basis: publication time of The Peninsula article (an upper bound of the announcement time)

sourceReferences.title: Temporary suspension of air navigation in Qatar
Qatar Airways special flights as Qatari airspace closure continues (7 March)

notVerified: Only press reports were captured; no QCAA statement or NOTAM.
Whether all flights or only some were suspended (exemptions) is not known.
Start and end times are not known.
events.confidenceNotes: Press only. Kept to show what was reported at the time, not as an established fact.

events.title: Doha Hamad International: suspension of all aircraft movements, as reported
events.titleJa: ドーハ・ハマド国際空港：全機の運航停止（報道による）
events.description: The Peninsula reports that Hamad International Airport confirmed the temporary suspension of all aircraft movements following the suspension of air navigation in Qatar.

publication.basis: publication time of The Peninsula article

sourceReferences.title: Hamad International Airport confirms temporary suspension of air traffic

notVerified: Start and end times are not known.
events.confidenceNotes: Airport-wide suspension as reported; whether runways were closed is not stated.

events.title: Kuwait: airspace and airport closed from 28 February, as reported
events.titleJa: クウェート：2月28日からの空域・空港の閉鎖（報道による）
events.description: Egypt Today reports (10 April) that the Kuwait Civil Aviation Authority denied a circulating announcement of resumed flights and that the airport had remained closed since 28 February.

effectiveFrom.basis: 'closed since February 28' in a report published on 10 April

effectiveUntil.basis: reopening reported for the evening of 23 April

sourceReferences.title: Kuwait's Civil Aviation Authority denies resumption of flights; airport remains closed since February 28
Kuwait reopens airspace starting this evening

notVerified: Press only; no Kuwaiti statement or NOTAM captured.
Whether some flights were allowed is not known.
The start date comes from a report written six weeks later.

events.title: Kuwait: phased reopening of the airspace, as reported
events.titleJa: クウェート：空域の段階的な再開（報道による）
events.description: The Peninsula reports that Kuwait's civil aviation director announced the reopening of the airspace from the evening of 23 April as part of a phased plan to resume air traffic.

publication.basis: publication time of The Peninsula article

sourceReferences.title: Kuwait reopens airspace starting this evening

notVerified: A phased reopening: it does not mean that operations returned to normal.

events.title: FAA SFAR 117: prohibition of flights in the Tehran FIR for U.S. operators
events.titleJa: FAA SFAR 117：米国の運航者によるテヘラン FIR での飛行の禁止
events.description: SFAR No. 117 (14 CFR 91.1617) prohibits flight operations in the Tehran FIR (OIIX) by U.S. air carriers, U.S. commercial operators, FAA airman certificate holders (except for a foreign air carrier) and operators of U.S.-registered aircraft (except foreign air carriers). A final rule published on 3 October 2024 extended it from 31 October 2024 to 31 October 2027. Listed on the FAA restrictions page in every capture from 12 February to 7 April 2026.

publication.basis: Federal Register issue date of the extension

effectiveUntil.basis: expiration date set by the extension

affectedOperators.text: U.S. air carriers and commercial operators, FAA certificate holders (except for foreign air carriers), U.S.-registered aircraft (except foreign air carriers)

sourceReferences.title: SFAR 117: Prohibition Against Certain Flights in the Tehran FIR (OIIX)
FAA Prohibitions, Restrictions and Notices (capture 2026-02-12)
FAA Prohibitions, Restrictions and Notices (capture 2026-03-01)
FAA Prohibitions, Restrictions and Notices (capture 2026-03-13)
FAA Prohibitions, Restrictions and Notices (capture 2026-04-07)

verified: The Federal Register text states the scope, the operators and the expiry.
events.confidenceNotes: Applies to U.S. operators only. It is not a closure of the Tehran FIR for other airlines.
